problemFraming.currentState: The People's Republic of China has intensified military, economic, and diplomatic coercion against Taiwan, conducting unprecedented military exercises in the Taiwan Strait, increasing gray-zone operations in the South China Sea, and leveraging economic dependencies to fracture alliance cohesion across the Indo-Pacific. USINDOPACOM maintains forward-deployed forces across the first and second island chains but faces sustainment challenges, basing access constraints, and competing global requirements. Regional allies are increasingly pressured by PRC economic leverage while simultaneously seeking stronger US security guarantees.
problemFraming.desiredEndState: PRC deterred from forceful reunification of Taiwan; Taiwan maintains de facto independence and ability to self-govern; US-led alliance network strengthened with enhanced interoperability and burden sharing; rules-based international order preserved in the Western Pacific; freedom of navigation and overflight maintained throughout the Indo-Pacific theater; escalation managed below the nuclear threshold.
problemFraming.problemStatement: How does USINDOPACOM deter PRC military coercion against Taiwan while maintaining regional stability, alliance cohesion, and freedom of navigation in the Indo-Pacific?
keyTensions: Deterrence posture risks provoking the escalation it seeks to prevent
Alliance cohesion requires burden sharing that not all partners can sustain
Forward presence depends on host-nation basing access subject to political shifts
Economic interdependence with PRC constrains partner willingness to impose costs
Information environment allows PRC narrative operations to undermine resolve
obstacles: PRC anti-access/area-denial (A2/AD) capabilities threaten freedom of maneuver within the first island chain
Logistics sustainment across vast Pacific distances limits operational endurance
Coalition national caveats restrict employment of partner forces
PRC escalation management doctrine differs from Western assumptions
Limited munitions stockpiles for high-intensity conflict
opportunities: Strengthened AUKUS partnership provides submarine and technology advantages
Enhanced bilateral defense agreements with Japan and Philippines expand basing options
PRC internal economic pressures constrain risk tolerance for military adventurism
Allied integrated air and missile defense networks create layered deterrence
Maritime domain awareness improvements enable persistent surveillance
assumptions: Japan provides basing access and logistical support under the US-Japan Security Treaty
Australia commits naval and air forces to South China Sea operations per AUKUS obligations
PRC leadership operates as a rational actor weighing costs against strategic objectives
No first-use nuclear policy holds for all parties through the conflict spectrum
Taiwan maintains will to resist and sustains critical infrastructure during crisis
Commercial shipping and air routes remain viable through the second island chain
constraints: Rules of engagement limit preemptive action to proportional response after hostile act/intent
Coalition partner national caveats restrict offensive operations in certain areas
Logistics sustainment requires 30-day operational stockpile at forward bases
Escalation management requires graduated response options at each phase
Cyber operations must avoid collateral effects on civilian critical infrastructure

root.label: Alliance Cohesion and Forward Basing Network
root.description: The integrated alliance network and forward-deployed force posture that enables power projection, deterrence credibility, and rapid response across the Indo-Pacific theater

children.label: Integrated Joint Force Projection
children.description: Ability to rapidly deploy, sustain, and employ joint forces across the Western Pacific from distributed basing locations

children.label: Forward Basing Access
children.description: Continued host-nation access to bases in Japan, Guam, Philippines, and Australia for force staging and sustainment

children.label: Host-Nation Political Will
children.description: Political shifts in allied nations could restrict or revoke basing access under PRC diplomatic or economic pressure

children.label: Theater Logistics Sustainment
children.description: Capacity to sustain high-intensity operations across 5,000+ nm supply lines from CONUS to the Western Pacific

children.label: Long Supply Lines
children.description: Extended logistics chains across the Pacific are vulnerable to PRC submarine interdiction and anti-ship missile targeting

children.label: Allied Interoperability
children.description: Ability to seamlessly integrate command, control, and fires across US, Japanese, Australian, and partner nation forces

children.label: Shared C2 Architecture
children.description: Common communication and data-sharing systems enabling multi-national force coordination

children.label: Classification Barriers
children.description: National classification systems and information sharing restrictions impede real-time coalition situational awareness

root.label: PRC Integrated Joint Force Projection Capability
root.description: The PLA's ability to project decisive military force across the Taiwan Strait through integrated joint operations combining naval, air, missile, cyber, and information warfare capabilities

children.label: Cross-Strait Amphibious Assault
children.description: Ability to transport, land, and sustain ground forces on Taiwan through amphibious and airborne operations

children.label: Air and Maritime Superiority over Taiwan Strait
children.description: PLA must achieve air and sea control over the 100nm Taiwan Strait corridor to protect amphibious forces

children.label: Concentrated Embarkation Points
children.description: Limited PLA Navy amphibious shipping must concentrate at predictable embarkation ports along the Fujian coast, creating targeting opportunities

children.label: Sealift Capacity
children.description: Sufficient military and requisitioned civilian sealift to transport 400,000+ troops and heavy equipment

children.label: Civilian Fleet Dependency
children.description: PLA relies on requisitioned civilian ro-ro ferries and container ships that are unarmored and vulnerable to attrition

children.label: A2/AD Denial Umbrella
children.description: Layered anti-access/area-denial capability using DF-21D/DF-26 anti-ship ballistic missiles, submarines, and integrated air defense to prevent US intervention

children.label: ISR and Targeting Chain
children.description: Persistent surveillance and real-time targeting data from satellites, over-the-horizon radar, and maritime patrol aircraft

children.label: Space-Based ISR Dependency
children.description: PLA kill chain depends on Yaogan satellite constellation for maritime targeting data — degradable through counterspace operations

linesOfEffort.name: Deter PRC Military Aggression
linesOfEffort.description: Demonstrate credible combat power and resolve to convince PRC leadership that the costs of military action against Taiwan outweigh any potential gains

decisivePoints.label: Forward Force Posture Established
decisivePoints.description: CSG and ESG positioned in Philippine Sea; THAAD and Patriot batteries active on Okinawa and Guam

decisivePoints.label: Maritime Domain Awareness Achieved
decisivePoints.description: Persistent ISR coverage of Taiwan Strait and PLA embarkation ports; submarine barrier patrols established

decisivePoints.label: PLA Amphibious Capability Denied
decisivePoints.description: Anti-ship fires neutralize PLA sealift concentration; cross-strait transit rendered untenable

linesOfEffort.name: Strengthen Alliance Network
linesOfEffort.description: Deepen bilateral and multilateral defense cooperation to present a unified coalition response and distribute the burden of Indo-Pacific security

decisivePoints.label: Coalition Command Structure Activated
decisivePoints.description: CJTF-WestPac operational with allied liaison officers; shared C2 systems verified

decisivePoints.label: Partner Force Integration Complete
decisivePoints.description: Japanese MSDF, Australian Navy, Philippine Navy integrated into theater maritime operations

decisivePoints.label: Burden Sharing Agreements Executed
decisivePoints.description: Allied nations sustaining agreed force contributions; logistics burden distributed across theater

linesOfEffort.name: Maintain Regional Stability
linesOfEffort.description: Prevent conflict spillover, maintain ASEAN engagement, and preserve economic alternatives to PRC dependency through targeted diplomatic and economic measures

decisivePoints.label: ASEAN Neutral Nations Engaged
decisivePoints.description: Diplomatic assurances and economic incentives prevent ASEAN neutrals from supporting PRC position

decisivePoints.label: Economic Alternatives Established
decisivePoints.description: Supply chain diversification and economic partnerships reduce regional PRC dependency

linesOfEffort.name: Information Operations
linesOfEffort.description: Counter PRC information warfare, support Taiwan societal resilience, and maintain international narrative supporting rules-based order

decisivePoints.label: Counter-Narrative Operations Active
decisivePoints.description: Coordinated strategic communications expose PRC disinformation and maintain allied domestic support

decisivePoints.label: Taiwan Societal Resilience Supported
decisivePoints.description: Civil defense coordination and information resilience programs sustain Taiwan population resolve

phases.name: Shape
phases.description: Establish conditions for deterrence through forward positioning, alliance engagement, and intelligence preparation. Build coalition readiness while avoiding premature escalation.

phases.name: Deter
phases.description: Demonstrate credible combat power and alliance resolve to convince PRC leadership that costs of aggression exceed gains. Signal through exercises, force movements, and diplomatic messaging.

phases.name: Seize Initiative
phases.description: If deterrence fails, rapidly transition to offensive operations to deny PRC fait accompli. Establish air and maritime superiority in the Philippine Sea and degrade PLA power projection.

phases.name: Dominate
phases.description: Achieve decisive conditions through sustained joint fires, interdiction of PLA logistics, and degradation of A2/AD capability. Enable conditions for conflict termination on favorable terms.

phases.name: Stabilize
phases.description: Transition to post-conflict stability operations. Restore freedom of navigation, reconstitute alliance posture, and support diplomatic resolution preserving Taiwan status quo.

conditions: PRC military activity exceeds normal exercise levels
Intelligence indicates increased PLA readiness posture
Diplomatic channels report hardening of PRC positions on Taiwan
PRC initiates kinetic action against Taiwan or allied forces
PLA crosses established red lines (blockade, missile strikes, airspace violation)
National command authority authorizes transition to combat operations
Initial PLA assault repelled or degraded below decisive threshold
Coalition forces achieve local air and maritime superiority
Allied force flow complete and sustaining operations
PRC accepts ceasefire or halts offensive operations
PLA force projection capability degraded below effective threshold
Diplomatic conditions for conflict termination established

decisionPoints.label: Transition to Active Deterrence
criteria: PRC military activity assessed as preparation for Taiwan contingency
Alliance consultation complete and partner commitments confirmed

decisionPoints.label: Authorization for Combat Operations
criteria: PRC hostile act or demonstrated hostile intent confirmed
National command authority authorizes use of force
Coalition partners notified and coordination complete

decisionPoints.label: Transition to Decisive Operations
criteria: Sufficient force flow to sustain extended operations
Intelligence confirms PLA commitment of reserve forces

decisionPoints.label: Accept Ceasefire Terms
criteria: Military conditions favorable for war termination

operationalApproach.narrative: USINDOPACOM executes a phased operational approach progressing from Shape through Stabilize to deter PRC military coercion against Taiwan. During the Shape phase, forward-deployed forces establish credible combat power across the first and second island chains while alliance integration deepens through bilateral exercises and shared C2 systems. As PRC provocations escalate, the Deter phase demonstrates resolve through visible force movements, expanded ISR coverage, and coordinated diplomatic messaging. If deterrence fails and PRC initiates military action, Seize Initiative rapidly transitions to offensive operations — prioritizing denial of PLA amphibious assault capability, degradation of the A2/AD umbrella through counterspace and anti-ship operations, and establishment of air superiority over the Philippine Sea. The Dominate phase sustains joint fires to attrit PLA force projection below decisive threshold while interdicting logistics flow across the Taiwan Strait. Throughout, Lines of Effort 2-4 (alliance strengthening, regional stability, information operations) reinforce the military line of effort by maintaining coalition unity, preventing conflict spillover to ASEAN neutrals, and countering PRC narrative operations. The Stabilize phase transitions to post-conflict posture reconstitution and diplomatic resolution preserving Taiwan's status quo and the rules-based international order.
